comments.text: The 5060's performance isn't bad, but its memory is intentionally limited to only 8GB. In 2025, I bought a 3060 because I don't have high gaming requirements; I wanted to play simple AI games, but my budget was limited (a brand new card plus about $200), so an NVIDIA card with 12GB of RAM was the bare minimum. Fortunately, the 3060, after being undervolted, lost a little performance but became more power-efficient and cooler. If I only play 1080p games and don't play AI games, the 5060 would probably be my first choice. (Of course, if my budget allowed, I would seriously consider the 4060 Ti 16GB or 5060 Ti 16GB; these two are the entry-level all-around graphics cards.)

I bought this rtx 5060 for $400 Canadian from an Indigenous store. I couldn’t be happier with my purchase. The cheapest 9060 xt 16gb is $520 (taxes included) which is the reaper model. After considering it all, I wanted hold onto my $120 and wanted to try out the 5060. 

Paired it with a 7600x and I’m getting some incredibly high fps in 1440p. When turning the dlss quality on, the fps goes even higher and somehow looks more visually appealing. Not to mention this Dlss thingy is pretty much available in every game, therefore allows the gamer to have seamless experience.

This card truly impressed me. I have the shadow model and the temps never exceeded 55-60 degrees and it’s dam silent. 

The lack of vram is unfortunate, and should be addressed by nvidia ASAP; Although people should give credit to nvidia for what they’ve done with this card… 20-30% uplift from the 4060 and also performing even better than the b580 while staying at the $300 price point, says a lot about this card.
